Subject: Request: Region-specific prompt/output/log removal (EU prod)

Hi Tessa,

We've completed our internal review and need Redwood to execute an erasure for a scoped set of artifacts stored/derived in our EU production tenant. This is an account-level request under our contract (see Section 5.2). Scope summary: 
- Prompts and assistant outputs tied to session IDs: FT-2026-ER-01 through FT-2026-ER-23
- Derived embeddings and vectors generated between 2026-06-01 and 2026-11-01
- Request logs and KV cache entries referencing those sessions

Environment: eu-west-1 (prod), customer namespace fintruity-prod. We need a chain-of-custody and attestations suitable for our compliance team (GDPR Article 17 impact). Please include expected runbook steps, an estimated maintenance window, and the type of deletion evidence you will provide (audit logs, manifests, signed attestation).

I've attached the formal request (fintruity_erasure_request_20261116.pdf). Can you confirm receipt and proposed timing?

Thanks,
Liam
Head of Security Operations
FinTruity

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.example

Subject: Re: Request: Region-specific prompt/output/log removal (EU prod)

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear scope and the attached PDF, we received it.

Proposed plan (high-level):
1) Identification: map the session IDs to S3 prefixes, KV cache prefixes, and embedding index buckets.
2) Pre-check: snapshot metadata (read-only) for audit, create runbook RW-842.
3) Execution window: 2026-11-18 02:00-03:00 UTC (low traffic window for eu-west-1).
4) Execution tasks: delete S3 objects, evict KV cache prefixes (prefix prune), remove embedding index shards, rotate related encryption keys (KMS) when applicable, and mark records in the deletion_manifest.csv.
5) Evidence collection: signed CSV manifest, tail snippets from the host audit log, and a brief attestation email.

Operational notes: we will run the KV cache sweep using the controlled prefix-prune tool (non-blocking), and model-variant fallbacks will be active so application traffic does not surface errors. Estimated downtime: none; minor latency blips possible.

To proceed we need: your confirmation of the proposed window, whether you require DocuSign acceptance, and whether you want on-prem-style hashed proofs or our standard manifest+audit snippets.

I'll loop in Vivek and Marcus to prepare RW-842.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Manager, Customer Security Ops
Redwood Inference

--

Tessa, Marcus —

We accept the proposed window: 2026-11-18 02:00-03:00 UTC.
A couple of requirements from our compliance team: 
- We need a DocuSign acceptance for the deletion manifest (signed by our DPO). Please send the link post-execution.
- Please include a short redaction confirmation for embeddings (we do not need the vectors preserved in any index form).
- Can you retain a minimal anonymized hash of the session IDs for seven days in case of audit requests? That hash should be non-reversible and stored in a restricted bucket.

If the runbook requires additional reviewers, let us know; otherwise we'll plan to sign after we receive your manifest and audit snippets.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Compliance Lead
FinTruity

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.example
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example, marcus_lin@redwood.example
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 01:30:05 +0000
Subject: [Action] RW-842 execution window starting now (eu-west-1) — follow steps, confirm completions

Team — executing RW-842 now for FinTruity. Ticket: INC-8942. Follow the checklist in RW-842 and call out when each step completes. Runbook excerpt below (condensed):

1) Lock the customer namespace in read-only mode for writes to session vectors (5 min prep).
2) Identify object prefixes: s3://fintruity-prod/prompts/session-FT-2026-ER-*/ and s3://fintruity-prod/outputs/session-FT-2026-ER-*/
3) Snapshot metadata for those prefixes to s3://redwood-audit/ft-2026-er/snapshots/20261118-0130.json (read-only).
4) Execute prefix-prune: /opt/redwood/bin/prefix_prune --bucket fintruity-prod --prefix "prompts/session-FT-2026-ER-" --dry-run false --manifest /tmp/deletion_manifest_20261118.csv
5) Evict KV caches: kvctl evict --namespace fintruity-prod --pattern "session-FT-2026-ER-*" --mode graceful
6) Remove embedding shards listed in embedding_shards_list.txt (use safe-delete to move to quarantine for 24h before hard delete)
7) Rotate KMS data key for any artifacts we flagged (if customer requested immediate key rotation)
8) Generate signed manifest and collect tail snippets from host audit logs (last 500 lines per host).

Questions: Marcus, is the safe-delete quarantine approach OK (move to quarantine for 24h then hard delete)? Laura, please prepare the attestation email template for the customer.

Reply-all with status updates.

Tessa

--
Attachment: RW-842-erasure-runbook-v1.md (text/markdown)
